messages.author: 0db2f7c09192585c
messages.subject: problematic ancestral ranges
parts:
Hi Nick,

 

I ran into several issues while running BioGeoBears. I had divided the distribution of the group into four areas: X, Y, Z, A. In the areas allowed matrix and areas adjacency matrix I have allowed only ancestral areas consisting of either: XY, XA or YZ. In the dispersal multipliers matrix, I have assigned zero dispersal probability from X to Z, Y to A and Z to A and vice versa and one to the rest (X to Y, X to A, Y to Z and vice versa). The max_range_size was 2. I shall list out the issues I have faced below:

1)    

 1    1) While running a DEC analysis, in a clade where all the tips were assigned the area X, one node showed distribution in A, and the range inheritance was: X/X. The node ancestor to the node in question had the distribution X.

2)   

 2    2) In another DEC analysis, although all the tip areas were either, X, Z, A or XY, the ancestral area of the root node was obtained as XY. The taxa distributed in X were present in every clade and there was also a solely X distributed clade sister to all other clades. In such situations one would expect the root node to be X.


3)    3) The plight continues as I divide the XY distributed tips into X and Y based on some preliminary species distribution analysis that I have done (still the root node has XY distribution).


4)    4)   I also ran an unconstrained analysis, where some ancestral areas were obtained as XYZ, although the max_range_size was 2.


It will be really great if you can suggest what is going wrong or what I have done wrong. If needed I shall send the tree and other files.


Thanks,

messages.author: 115d05260b0c341a
messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] problematic ancestral ranges
parts:
Hi -- #4 is probably a mistake in your script or in copying/pasting, it's impossible to get XYZ if max_range_size is 2.  The others sound like problems of interpretation -- biogeography algorithms work different than your standard intuitions gained from standard parsimony or standard continuous-time ML ancestral state inferences.

I can't say more unless you send the files...cheers!
Nick
